items.stem: Why does scooping flour straight from the bag with the measuring cup often give a dry, dense cake?

options.text: Scooping is the most accurate way to measure flour, so that is not the cause
Scooping fluffs the flour up, so the cup holds too little flour
Scooping packs the flour down, so the cup holds too much flour

items.stem: A recipe calls for 250 g of flour. One cup of spooned-and-leveled flour weighs about 125 g. How many cups is that?
What does "spoon and level" mean when you measure flour?
What should you use to measure 1 cup of milk?

options.text: A liquid measuring cup, read at eye level on a flat counter
A dry measuring cup filled until it looks about full
A coffee mug, since a cup is a cup

items.stem: Why is weighing ingredients more accurate than measuring them with cups?
The recipe says 2 teaspoons of baking powder, and you add 2 heaping teaspoons. Does it matter?

options.text: No, a little extra is fine in baking
Yes: small amounts of leavener matter, and too much makes the cake rise fast and then collapse, or taste bitter
Only if the cake is chocolate
